who: Historian of ancient Rome at the University of Massachusetts Amherst; PhD Berkeley 1984.

evidence.says: UMass History identifies Carlin Barton as professor emerita specializing in ancient Rome, with a Berkeley PhD (1984).
The authority for Carlin A. Barton cites Roman Honor and identifies its author as professor of history at UMass Amherst.

notes: The candidate authority, institution, field and exact doctorate institution/year agree.

who: Historian of Canadian social and business history; Victoria professor emeritus and Alberta research chair; PhD Queen’s 1973.

evidence.says: The Peter A. Baskerville authority also records Peter Baskerville and identifies him as an associate professor of history at Victoria.
The 2016 university announcement identifies Peter Baskerville as Alberta research chair and Victoria professor emeritus.
Baskerville’s article cites his dissertation, The boardroom and beyond, as a Queen’s University PhD thesis (1973).
Murray’s dissertation, p. ii, lists Peter A. Baskerville of Alberta as outside committee member; Eric W. Sager is supervisor.

notes: Identity confirmed, but the dissertation qualifies the AHA advisor role: Baskerville was outside committee member, not the named supervisor.

who: Historian of modern China and South Asia at UC Santa Cruz; doctoral studies at Berkeley.

evidence.says: The Dilip K. Basu authority records the variant Dilip Basu and identifies the UC Santa Cruz humanities professor and Satyajit Ray collection director.
UCSC reports Basu joined its history faculty in 1971 and completed his Berkeley dissertation on Asian merchants and Western trade in 1974.
The department’s alumni listing names Dilip Basu as Maia Ramnath’s faculty advisor.

notes: LC explicitly joins the short and expanded names. UCSC reports dissertation completion in 1974, whereas AHA lists the doctorate in 1975; that year difference remains unresolved.

who: Historian of modern Italy and fascism at New York University; PhD in comparative history, Brandeis.

evidence.says: Her CV identifies the NYU historian and Brandeis doctorate; p. 17 lists Malandrucco’s Chicago history PhD (December 2016), co-chaired with Moishe Postone, on labor and the 1942 Rome exposition.
The candidate item identifies Ruth Ben-Ghiat, NYU employment, Brandeis education and LC authority no96042061.

notes: Direct supervision evidence explains the Chicago student despite her NYU affiliation; the dissertation title is worded differently in the CV.

who: Historian of modern France at the University of Virginia; PhD Johns Hopkins 1973.

evidence.says: The Lenard R. Berlanstein authority identifies a Virginia history professor specializing in modern France.
The AHA memorial describes his study at Johns Hopkins and teaching at Virginia for 38 years beginning in fall 1973.
History doctorate: Johns Hopkins, 1973.

notes: The candidate’s authority, field, doctorate and Virginia appointment through the student’s 2011 completion agree.

who: Historian of visual culture and medicine; New Brunswick history faculty 1996–2007, then Alberta; PhD Rochester 1996.

evidence.says: The Lianne McTavish authority identifies an associate professor of visual culture in New Brunswick’s history department.
Her CV records the Rochester PhD and New Brunswick appointments; p. 33 lists co-direction of Heather Molyneaux’s New Brunswick PhD on medical advertisements and women, defended 2009.

notes: Explicit co-direction confirms the identity despite her move to Alberta before the defense; the CV uses a variant dissertation title.

who: Arthur Eugene Bestor, historian of the United States at the University of Washington, Seattle.

evidence.says: The Arthur Eugene Bestor authority records Arthur Bestor as professor emeritus of history at Washington, Seattle, and a faculty appointment beginning in 1963.
The AHA memorial states that Belz earned his Washington PhD in 1966 under Arthur Bestor; it identifies the dissertation subsequently published as Reconstructing the Union.

notes: Direct student supervision evidence and the candidate’s authority identify the same Washington historian.

who: Henry Stuart Hughes, historian of modern European intellectual history at Harvard; Harvard PhD 1940.

evidence.says: The H. Stuart (Henry Stuart) Hughes authority identifies the historian of modern Europe and records his Harvard PhD (1940).
Identifies Henry Stuart Hughes as Harvard history professor, teaching there in 1948–1952 and 1957–1975, including the student’s 1963 completion.
The alternative authority is headed Heather Hughes and cites Imijondolo (1985), not H. Stuart Hughes.

notes: Select p-105951. Reject p-109593 (Heather Hughes), a different author; the matching authority and Harvard appointment identify Henry Stuart Hughes.
